facts.statement: The genus contains three species: G. aptiensis, G. magnus, and G. dentatus.
facts.quote: It contains three species: Gladioserratus aptiensis Pictet, 1865 Gladioserratus magnus Underwood, Goswami, Prasad, Verma & Flynn, 2011 Gladioserratus dentatus Guinot, Cappetta & Adnet, 2014

facts.statement: The original authors described the genus as containing species that lived from the Hauterivian to the Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: The authors of its description considered it to be an exclusively Cretaceous genus, containing species living from Hauterivian to Cenomanian.

facts.statement: The species G. dentatus was described from fossils found in the Valanginian of France.
facts.quote: Subsequently the species G. dentatus was described from the Valanginian of France.

facts.statement: Teeth found in the middle Danian Faxe Formation at Faxe, Denmark, extend the genus's known range into the Paleocene.
facts.quote: Teeth described by Adolfssen and Ward (2015), collected from the middle Danian Faxe Formation at Faxe, Denmark, extend the temporal range of the genus to Paleocene

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that assigning Notorynchus serratissimus to Gladioserratus would extend the genus's range to the early Eocene.
facts.quote: according to the authors, the species "Notorynchus" serratissimus Agassiz (1843) should probably be assigned to the genus Gladioserratus as well, which, if confirmed, would further extended the temporal range of the genus to the early Eocene.

facts.statement: Gladioserratus belongs to the family Hexanchidae.
Gladioserratus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus lived from 137.05 to 61.66 million years ago, spanning the Valanginian to Danian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Danian (137.05 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 64 recorded fossil occurrences of Gladioserratus.

rejected.statement: Gladioserratus is an extinct genus of cow shark.
rejected.quote: Gladioserratus is an extinct genus of cow shark.
